ambiguities.ruling: RULED --balance none (ratified) — three grounds: the card's own §3 arithmetic, L0 anchor comparability, and confound control.
ambiguities.where: design §4 `splits` vs design §3 "Pool survival" — the two sections of the registered card disagree
ambiguities.question: §4 says "pools subsampled to common per-class n within each level (discards logged)". §3 states the realized pools as "L1 ~3.5k (math) – 24k (alpaca)". Those cannot both hold: a common per-class n is ONE number per level, not a 7x range.
ambiguities.resolution: --balance none (default). MEASURED, not argued: this script computes L1's per-class training pools as 2,628 (math steps_ge4) – 24,788 (alpaca no_input), which reproduces §3's stated "~3.5k – 24k" exactly; no other policy does (--balance task gives 2,628 – 14,212, --balance level gives 2,628 everywhere). §3 therefore describes an UNBALANCED build, and §4's sentence is the part of the card that does not fit its own arithmetic. Second, independent reason: L0's 240 adapters already exist and were trained on unbalanced pools (6,973 – 40,000). Balancing L1 would move TWO variables between the curve's first two points — K and pool policy — and level-wide balancing would additionally raise every L1 class from ~1.3 epochs to 12.18, inflating the very memorization confound §9.2 names and D7 exists to test.
alternatives: --balance level (the literal §4 sentence; discards 82.5% of L1's training rows)
--balance task (within-task common n; discards 6.6% at L1)
ambiguities.consequence: Under `none`, per-class pool size varies WITHIN a level, so epochs-per-pool vary within a level (reported per class, as §9.2 requires). Realized n and discarded mass under all three policies are computed and reported for every level, so the choice is a one-flag re-run.

ambiguities.ruling: ACCEPTED PROVISIONALLY — Director review of the authored taxonomy required before L2 fires. No effect on L1.
ambiguities.where: design §3 table, alpaca L2/L3: "4 / 8 instruction-verb families [T2 keyword rules]"
ambiguities.question: The card names the tier and the count but not the rules: which verb families, and which verbs in each.
ambiguities.resolution: Meridian-authored frozen taxonomy (ALPACA_VERB_L3, 8 families over the instruction's first word, with a residual `other`; L2 = the frozen pairwise merge ALPACA_VERB_L2_MERGE, so L2 is a strict coarsening of L3).
alternatives: a data-driven clustering (would make the cells T3)
ambiguities.consequence: This is an authored label space inside a registered card. It should be reviewed before the L2/L3 tiers fire; it does not affect L1 (alpaca L1 is native).

ambiguities.ruling: RULED as built — four named languages, residual discarded and logged. No effect on L1.
ambiguities.where: design §3 table, code L2/L3: "output language {Python / non-Python / …} [T2; skew audit]"
ambiguities.question: Which four language classes, and what happens to the mass that matches none of them (measured: 43% of the CodeAlpaca pool matches no language marker).
ambiguities.resolution: four NAMED languages (sql, html_css, javascript, python) under a frozen ordered-pattern rule; the residual is DISCARDED and its mass logged.
alternatives: make the residual a 4th class (`other`) — zero discard, but the class's definition is 'everything else', which the D6 data-space reference would correctly read as inseparable
ambiguities.consequence: The discarded mass is logged per level. `sql` is the binding class for code's floor — its realized n is reported.

ambiguities.ruling: RULED doc-length median [T2] (ratified) — L1 is then 12/12 clean-core and annotator-free.
ambiguities.where: design §3 table, xsum L1: "doc-length median [T2, weak] or 2 topics [T3]"
ambiguities.question: The card offers two options and does not choose.
ambiguities.resolution: doc-length median [T2]. L1 is then 12/12 clean-core, needs no annotator, and can launch immediately — which matters because L1 is the only funded tier after L0.
alternatives: 2 model-annotated topics [T3] — would make L1's clean-core curve 10/12 classes
ambiguities.consequence: The L1 all-classes and clean-core curves coincide exactly, so the D3 divergence rule has nothing to bite on at L1. Stated in the L1 readout.

ambiguities.ruling: STOP CONFIRMED — L2/L3 stay unlaunchable until a dated amendment pins model id + prompt + inventory + procedure + seed.
ambiguities.where: design §3 table, xsum L2 (4 topics) and L3 (12 topics), both [T3 model-annotated]
ambiguities.question: The card admits T3 cells (D3 RESTRICTED) but pins NO annotator: no model, no prompt, no topic inventory, no frozen assignment procedure exists in the record.
ambiguities.resolution: STOP. xsum's L2/L3 classes are DECLARED but NOT MATERIALIZED (status pending_t3_annotation, no row ids). Every other class at L2/L3 is materialized. L2 and L3 are NOT launchable until an annotator is pinned by dated amendment.
alternatives: pin an annotator (model id + prompt + inventory + seed) as a dated amendment
substitute a T2 rule (e.g. length quantiles), which changes the semantic axis the card names and would make the whole ladder clean-core
ambiguities.consequence: K=24 at L2 and K=48 at L3 both DEPEND on xsum: without it L2 realizes K=20 and L3 realizes K=36. This gates the L2 and L3 tiers only; L0, L1 and Arm B are unaffected.

ambiguities.ruling: RULED 16/8/4/3 at rungs 2/4/8/16 (= 144 runs exactly) — the card's 2->16 span wins over constant-N.
ambiguities.where: design §11 item 8 / D8 PROMOTED: "squad-only deep ladder, 2->16 native title groups, ~144 runs"
ambiguities.question: The TOTAL is fixed — the locked cost table gives Arm B 3.056 GPU-days, which at the measured 30.56 min/run is exactly 144.0 runs — but the per-rung seed allocation is unspecified.
ambiguities.resolution: seeds 16/8/4/3 at rungs 2/4/8/16 = 32+32+32+48 = 144 runs exactly, preserving the card's stated 2->16 span and its stated total.
alternatives: rungs 4/8/16 at a constant N=48 per rung (= 144 exactly, honours D2's constant-N rationale, but drops the 2-group rung the card names)
ambiguities.consequence: Classifier N is 32/32/32/48 rather than constant across rungs, so Arm B's curve is not sample-size-matched the way the main ladder's is. Reported.

ambiguities.ruling: RULED largest-pool T1 L2 class, halves from the FULL class pool.
ambiguities.where: design §6.2 / D7 MANDATORY: "One L2 class: adapters on two disjoint halves of the same pool (5 + 5 seeds)"
ambiguities.question: Which L2 class; and are the halves halves of the FULL class pool or of the level-balanced pool (under G-1's level-wide balancing, half a balanced pool falls below the D4 floor).
ambiguities.resolution: the largest-pool T1-tier L2 class (deterministic, recorded); halves are taken from the class's FULL training pool, so each half clears the D4 floor. D7 is a control, not a level cell — it is not level-balanced, and says so.
alternatives: a small-pool class (sharper memorization test, but halves may fall below the floor)
ambiguities.consequence: D7's two half-pools are ~half the size of the full class pool and therefore see ~2x the epochs of the unbalanced class. Reported with the control.

ambiguities.where: design §3 table L3 (xsum "8–12 topics", squad "8–16 title groups") vs the lock's "L3 ~48x5"
ambiguities.question: The card gives ranges; the lock gives ~48 classes and 240 adapters at 5 seeds.
ambiguities.resolution: xsum 12 + squad 16, with alpaca 8, code 4, math 4, agnews 4 -> K = 48 exactly, 48 x 5 = 240 adapters. This is the only combination inside the card's stated ranges that hits the lock's numbers exactly.
alternatives: any other point in the ranges, at the cost of K != 48 and adapters != 240
ambiguities.consequence: L3's realized K depends on G-5 being resolved; without xsum, L3 realizes K=36.
ambiguities.authority: recorded derivation (no ruling needed unless contested)

ambiguities.where: design §3 "training pool >= 1,000 examples" vs §4 "per-CLASS fixed 500-example val"
ambiguities.question: Is the D4 floor measured before or after the per-class val is removed.
ambiguities.resolution: after — the floor is read literally as a floor on the TRAINING pool, so a class needs >= 1,500 pool rows to be eligible.
alternatives: floor on the pre-val class pool (a 1,000-row class would train on 500 examples = 64 epochs)
ambiguities.consequence: The stricter reading. Eligibility is reported with both counts (n_class_rows and n_train_pool).
